top10.introHtml: Refreshed 2026-09-24. Showing top 4-seat convertibles within 35 mi of Media, PA, $7k–$15k. Sources: Cars.com (10 listings post-filter / 23 found), CarGurus (21 listings post-filter / 37 found), AutoTrader (19 listings post-filter / 53 found). Excludes 2-seat roadsters (Miata, Z3/Z4, Boxster, SLK, TT, Crossfire, Thunderbird 2002–2005, Allante). Personal excludes: MINI, Buick, Volvo, Toyota Solara, Camaro, pre-2005 Mustangs. TrueCar body-style filter broken — zeroed out.

picks.whyGood: The G37 Convertible is one of the sharpest-looking soft-tops in budget. VQ37VHR V6 makes 325 hp, 7-speed auto is smooth, and the rear 2+2 seats are genuinely usable for adults on short trips. Faulkner Infiniti is a franchise dealer — clean title + no accidents on Cars.com, 91k miles on a VQ engine that routinely goes 200k with oil changes. Factory hard-top mechanism is robust. Media PA flagship dealer means you can actually get service.
picks.whatToVerify: Full power-top cycle (open and close twice); check headliner for water stains at A-pillars; rear window defroster function; rocker panel rust (common after 10+ winters); VQ timing chain tensioners (rattle on cold start = attention needed); differential fluid age.
picks.bottomLine: The best all-around pick — sporty V6 power, franchise-dealer provenance, and a convertible top that actually folds into a proper trunk lid.

picks.whyGood: S550-generation Mustang (2015–2023) is the modern benchmark. The EcoBoost 2.3T makes 310 hp, better real-world mpg than the GT, and the SelectShift 10-speed auto is slick. CarGurus rates it 'Great Price' at $10,995 — that's a lot of convertible for the money. Fred Beans is a volume Ford dealer in Langhorne, likely off a trade-in with full service history. 132k miles is high but the 2.3T EcoBoost is a known truck/Bronco engine built for longevity.
picks.whatToVerify: Power-top full cycle; rear-seat water staining (common if top seal leaks); check for rear-camera function and SYNC updates; oil consumption test at idle; transmission fluid color; any deferred TSB for EcoBoost carbon buildup.
picks.bottomLine: Most car per dollar — modern safety tech, 310 hp, and a 'Great Price' flag from CarGurus make this the smart buy if mileage doesn't scare you.

picks.whyGood: 40k miles on a 2012 BMW is practically new for the platform. The N52 inline-6 in the 128i is bulletproof — naturally aspirated, simple VANOS, no turbos to blow. Selden Motors at Willow Grove is a well-known used BMW specialist. Clean title + no accidents on Cars.com. At $14,140 you're paying a premium but getting a unicorn-mileage E88 that should be drama-free for years.
picks.whatToVerify: Check for any deferred 60k-mile maintenance (coolant, brake fluid, plugs, cabin filter); power-folding top latches; rear window defroster; cooling system pressure test (plastic fittings age); check for wheel corrosion.
picks.bottomLine: If you want peace of mind over price, this low-mile 128i is the answer — properly sorted BMW that will need almost nothing for the next 50k miles.

picks.whyGood: The A205 C-Class Cabriolet is the most elegant car in the budget — Airscarf neck heating, Magic Sky sliding roof panel, and a refined 2.0T 9-speed combo. 4MATIC AWD is a rare find on a convertible. Cars.com verifies clean title and no accidents. Burlington NJ is close enough for a day trip. 104k miles on a C-Class is normal operating hours for this platform.
picks.whatToVerify: Magic Sky roof panel function (expensive to replace); Airscarf operation; engine oil leaks at valve cover gaskets (common 276-engine issue); 7G-Tronic fluid condition; check panoramic canvas top mechanism; any active Takata airbag recalls.
picks.bottomLine: For the buyer who wants refinement over raw performance — the most sophisticated convertible in the search at this price point. Worth the trip to Burlington.

picks.whyGood: The Audi A5 Cabriolet is often overlooked in BMW/Mercedes budget debates, but the 2.0T quattro AWD is a real all-season convertible. The B8.5 refresh (2012–2017) fixed most early quirks. 91k miles on the EA888 Gen2 engine is middle-aged. $10,800 is fair money for a 2014 AWD Audi cabriolet.
picks.whatToVerify: EA888 oil consumption test (pour 1 qt, drive 1k miles, check again); timing chain tensioner service history (2.0T weakness pre-2013, improved on 2014); HVAC blower motor; quattro rear differential fluid; convertible top rear seal inspection.
picks.bottomLine: The sleeper pick — quattro AWD sets it apart from every other convertible in this budget. If the EA888 checks out, this is a serious all-weather car.

picks.whyGood: 35k miles on a 2001 CLK 430 is museum territory. The M113 4.3L V8 is naturally aspirated Mercedes iron — these engines routinely clear 200k+ with regular oil changes. Selden Motors is a known specialist dealer in Willow Grove. Clean title + no accidents on Cars.com.
picks.whatToVerify: Check for SRS airbag recall completeness (CLK430 had multiple Takata campaigns); hydraulic soft-top fluid level and pump motor; rear window defroster grid; subframe rust inspection (2001 era exposed frame rails); check all 4 windows seal for water infiltration.
picks.bottomLine: 35k-mile V8 CLK from a specialist dealer — if the Takata recalls are cleared and the top works, this is a genuine collectors find at $12,480.

picks.whyGood: The last CLK 350 Cabriolet before Mercedes went to the E-Class Cabriolet platform — a cleaner, simpler car than the later E-Class. 65k miles on the M272 3.5L V6 is barely half its service life. Located in Media, PA — right next door (2 miles). Prime Autohaus is a known local independent.
picks.whatToVerify: M272 balance shaft failure (2006–2008 built engines had the issue; check build date vs 2009 MY); hydraulic soft-top fluid and pump; check for any rust around drain channels; verify convertible-top boot snap retention; power windows full up/down test.
picks.bottomLine: The local pick — 2 miles from 19063, 65k miles on an elegant V6, and a specialist dealer. Makes test drives and post-purchase service trivially easy.

picks.whyGood: The A3 Cabriolet (8V) is the entry-level German convertible with modern electronics — Apple CarPlay area, Virtual Cockpit-compatible, and the most current safety tech in this budget. 84k miles on the EA888 Gen3 (2016 revision) is well within normal. Clean title + no accidents, private seller in Plymouth Meeting.
picks.whatToVerify: EA888 Gen3 oil consumption (improved but still worth testing); canvas top rear-window delamination check; check for DSG/S-Tronic service at 40k intervals; HVAC actuator function; CarFax for any prior ownership gaps.
picks.bottomLine: The modern-features pick — if Apple CarPlay and virtual gauges matter to you, the A3 Cabriolet is years ahead of the other cars here. Surprisingly practical daily driver.

picks.whyGood: The CLK 500 is the V8-powered sleeper of this list — M113 5.0L naturally aspirated, 302 hp, and 82k miles on an engine that's essentially indestructible. $7,900 for a Mercedes V8 cabriolet is a genuine deal. Private Seller Exchange listings are consignment but prices are often sharper than dealer.
picks.whatToVerify: Hydraulic soft-top full cycle test; check for rust in subframe rail channels (NJ car, winter salt exposure); SRS airbag recall completeness; M113 spark plug access (8 plugs, rear bank is awkward); check for any oil leaks from rear main seal.
picks.bottomLine: Best bang for buck in V8 territory — $7,900 for 302hp Mercedes cabriolet. Budget for a pre-purchase inspection and you have the deal of the search.

picks.whyGood: The F33 435i xDrive is the most powerful car in this top 10 — N55 turbocharged inline-6, 300 hp, and xDrive AWD. AutoTrader badges it 'Great Deal'. At $8,500 for a 2015 BMW with all-wheel drive, you're getting an incredible amount of engineering. High miles at 140k but the N55 is a robust architecture that routinely goes 200k+.
picks.whatToVerify: N55 oil filter housing gasket (notorious leak at this mileage); xDrive transfer case fluid; power-folding hard-top mechanism (4-piece folding roof is mechanically complex); check cooling system for any bubbling; iDrive logic board function; tire wear pattern for alignment history.
picks.bottomLine: The performance wild card — xDrive AWD + 300hp at $8,500 is exceptional value. High miles mean you need a PPI, but this could be the star of the search.

manual10.introHtml: Manual-transmission convertibles only. BMWs in this era (E46, E93, E88) were available with 5- or 6-speed Getrag boxes. Verify by VIN before driving out — many listings omit transmission. Eclipse Spyder GT was offered in 5-speed manual with the 3.0L V6. Call ahead to confirm stick shift.

picks.whyGood: The E93 335i was offered in a 6-speed manual — one of BMW's last great manual convertibles before the brand went full-auto. Twin-scroll N54 turbo makes 300 hp. CarVision of Trooper is a known pre-owned specialist. Under $10k for a 335i convertible is hard to find.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm manual (request VIN decode or window sticker — CarVision listing may be auto but many of these 335i convertibles come through in manual); N54 high-pressure fuel pump (known failure at 80–100k); charge pipe end caps; waste-gate rattle on cold start; rod bearing inspection.
picks.bottomLine: If it's a manual, this is the sports-pick of the list — 300hp twin-turbo inline-6 with a proper gearbox, at $10k.

picks.whyGood: The 3G Eclipse Spyder GT was offered in a 5-speed manual with the 3.0L SOHC V6. Low-ish miles at 71k. Clean title + no accidents on Cars.com. The 3G Eclipse is the JDM era — FWD but with genuine sport character. Manual makes it feel more connected than the automatic version.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm 5-speed manual (ask Meric for VIN decode or door sticker — GT came in auto or manual); timing belt service history (interference engine — critical); power-soft-top hydraulic pump condition; check for any head gasket weeping; clutch pedal travel and engagement point.
picks.bottomLine: If it's the 5-speed, this Eclipse Spyder GT is the most affordable driver's pick on the manual tab — fun, low-miles FWD sport convertible.

picks.whyGood: The E88 128i was available in a 6-speed manual — BMW's last great analog convertible before the F-series. N52 naturally aspirated inline-6 is the most reliable engine BMW has ever made. SULEV designation means extra-clean emissions tuning. At $7,485 this is the budget floor for a BMW convertible.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm manual (listing says automatic, but verify — many 128i convertibles come in both; this listing may be auto); N52 VANOS oil control solenoid (rattle on cold start = sticky vanos); power-folding top full cycle; inspect rear subframe carrier bushings; check for any FC from SULEV emissions system.
picks.bottomLine: The bargain floor of the BMW convertible market — $7,485 for a natural-aspirated BMW inline-6 soft-top. Verify the transmission first; if it's the 6-speed, this is a steal.

picks.whyGood: The E46 325Ci is arguably the best manual convertible BMW ever made — perfectly balanced, sub-3,500 lb, and the 2.5L inline-6 with a 5-speed Getrag is an engineering treasure. 57k miles on a 2006 is remarkably clean. Clean title + no accidents at Car Cheer.
picks.whatToVerify: Confirm manual transmission — critical to verify by VIN; E46 subframe reinforcement (rear subframe cracking is an E46 known issue, especially on convertibles — inspect welds); check cooling system (plastic fittings age on E46); convertible top hydraulic cylinder seal condition; front control arm bushings.
picks.bottomLine: If it's a 5-speed, this is arguably the best drivers' pick in the entire search — the E46 325Ci is a classic. Pay for a pre-purchase inspection without question.

mustangs.introHtml: Ford Mustang convertibles only, 2005+ (S197 fifth-gen and newer). Excludes every SN-95 and Fox-body regardless of condition. All years shown are soft-top convertibles — no fastbacks or coupes in results.

picks.whyGood: 2020 is the freshest Mustang in budget — S550 generation, EcoBoost 2.3T at 310 hp, SelectShift 10-speed auto. CarGurus 'Great Price' flag at $10,995 from a Ford dealer with service history. Still under 7 years old so most OEM part support is strong.
picks.whatToVerify: Power-top full open/close cycle (listen for motor strain); rear-seat water staining from top seal; carbon buildup on EcoBoost intake valves (check service records for any catch-can or walnut blast); transmission fluid color; any SYNC recall completeness.
picks.bottomLine: Best Mustang value in the search — 'Great Price' rated, franchise dealer, modern safety tech. The smart buy for someone who wants current-gen Mustang fun.

picks.whyGood: S197 generation (2005–2014) — the last of the retro-style Mustangs. V6 Pentastar 3.7L at 305 hp. AutoTrader rates it 'Great Deal' at $8,952. Josie's in Gilbertsville is a high-volume independent. 121k miles is mid-life for the Cyclone/Modular platform.
picks.whatToVerify: Soft-top rear window seal (plastic yellowing is common); check for any transmission shudder at part-throttle (V6 Mustang 6-speed is finicky); listen for differential whine on acceleration/decel; rocker panel rust (inspect the S197 lower sills carefully in salt-state cars); CarFax for any unreported events.
picks.bottomLine: Entry-level Mustang convertible under $9k — 305 hp V6 with a proper pony-car look. The roof and floor are what to watch; mechanically these are simple, robust cars.
